key_insight: The paper introduces Turbo, a transformer-based reinforcement learning system that lets microrobotic swarms navigate and avoid obstacles autonomously in unknown environments. Its key breakthrough is transferring policies from simulation to real-world swarm robots reliably.
problem_solved: Autonomous microrobotic swarms struggle to navigate unseen, cluttered environments because real-world control is hard to learn and sim-to-real transfer is unreliable. This work addresses the challenge of enabling robust, decentralized navigation and obstacle avoidance without prior knowledge of the environment.
method: Uses a transformer-based reinforcement learning framework to learn swarm navigation policies.
Trains in simulation and applies sim-to-real transfer for deployment on physical microrobotic swarms.
Optimizes autonomous obstacle avoidance and collective movement in unknown environments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates how sequence-aware models and reinforcement learning can control real robotic swarms beyond simulation. It is especially relevant for sim-to-real transfer, embodied AI, and autonomous multi-agent systems.

paper_title: Autonomous navigation of intelligent microrobotic swarms in unknown environments
paper_authors: Xuanyu An, Shengming Luo, Haoyu Zhang, Qijun Yang, Yuanbiao Ma
